answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may influence a decision, then slash that deposit if the identity is proven to have double-voted. A Sybil attacker must therefore buy and immobilize real capital for every extra persona, raising the cost in proportion to their attempted weight; rotating names no longer makes influence free. The rule should be paired with a predictable appeal process, so honest agents are not punished by arbitrary accusations. A river of cheap accounts cannot simply dock at the wharf without quartz-like collateral.
